questions.question: What is the primary challenge in synchronizing physical clocks in a distributed system?
options: The clocks are too fast
The clocks are too slow
The clocks drift at different rates
The clocks are not accessible
questions.answer: The clocks drift at different rates

questions.question: In the context of clock synchronization, what is a 'time server'?
options: A server that serves web pages
A server that provides a reference time
A server that stores files
A server that runs a database
questions.answer: A server that provides a reference time

questions.question: What is the main idea behind Cristian's algorithm?
options: To slow down all clocks
To speed up all clocks
To adjust a client's clock based on a server's time and network delay
To stop all clocks
questions.answer: To adjust a client's clock based on a server's time and network delay

questions.question: How does NTP handle the variability of network delay?
options: It ignores it
It assumes a constant delay
It uses statistical methods to filter measurements
It asks the user to input the delay
questions.answer: It uses statistical methods to filter measurements

questions.question: What is the purpose of the hierarchical structure of NTP servers?
options: To make the system more complex
To distribute the load and improve accuracy
To make the system less reliable
To make the system more expensive
questions.answer: To distribute the load and improve accuracy

questions.question: If a client receives a timestamp from a server, what else does it need to consider before setting its clock?
options: The server's location
The network round-trip time
The server's uptime
The number of users on the server

questions.question: Why is it generally not a good idea to simply set a client's clock backward if it's ahead of the server's time?
options: It can cause events to appear to happen in the past
It can damage the clock hardware
It can cause the server to crash
It can violate the laws of physics
questions.answer: It can cause events to appear to happen in the past

questions.question: How can a system handle the issue of a clock being set backward?
options: By always setting the clock forward
By gradually slowing down the clock until it's correct
By ignoring the server's time
By shutting down the system
questions.answer: By gradually slowing down the clock until it's correct

questions.question: What is the trade-off between synchronization frequency and network traffic?
options: More frequent synchronization leads to less traffic
More frequent synchronization leads to more traffic
There is no trade-off
The trade-off depends on the time of day
questions.answer: More frequent synchronization leads to more traffic
